quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down to let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Dogs are attracted to motorcycles. If chased, slow down and let the dog approach. Then accelerate and leave the dog behind.

questions.question: Your normal scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Always looking in the rearview mirror.
Checking the rearview mirror often.
Not using the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while riding. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while crossing uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Downshift to a lower gear right away.
Zigzag across the bridge.
Relax and steer straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and steer straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on uneven gratings, stay relaxed and go straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must stay within the speed limit.
Must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it may cause the bike to tip. Use only the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not recommended because you cannot get used to any part of a lane.
Not recommended because it confuses other drivers.
Good practice when road and traffic conditions change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good practice when road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, change gears to:

options.text: Avoid sudden power changes in the middle of the turn.
Keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden power changes in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start turning. Shifting during a turn can cause sudden power changes that may skid the rear wheel. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, instruct them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before starting the engine.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Avoid unnecessary talking or movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid unnecessary talking or movement.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move unnecessarily while riding. Passengers should board after the engine starts. They should sit forward, not back, without crowding the operator.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Need less stopping room than larger vehicles.
Need the same stopping room as larger vehicles.
Can stop instantly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need the same stopping room as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need as much stopping distance as other vehicles. Always keep enough space to stop safely based on conditions.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher is considered intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. Intoxicated people cannot legally operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: When lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is put on the back of slow-moving vehicles going slower than 25 mph. Examples include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When being passed, where should motorcyclists ride in the lane?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing driver creates danger for both of you.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can steer with your arms, not hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly when holding the handlebars. Press your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn is ________ a car horn.

options.text: Louder than
Quieter than
About as loud as

questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: Motorcycle horns are not as loud as car horns. Use your horn when needed, but do not depend on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing. This gives you a better view and helps drivers in the next lane see your move.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride wherever you are most comfortable.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid car doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Be ready to change position as needed.

questions.question: If parked vehicles are on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to avoid opening doors and people stepping out. If oncoming traffic is present, stay in the center to have more space around you.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may signal the passing driver to move back into your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: Your rear wheel locks up while you stop on dry pavement. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then apply it again quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on dry pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle stays under control if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, where in your lane should you ride?

options.text: Right side
Center
Left side

questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when being passed. Riding near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding far from it may make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when safe.
Stop only if other traffic is coming.
Other vehicles are entering the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic flows both ways
Right lane is ending
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose your lane position based on conditions and adjust as needed.
